key_insight: Zero-shot LLMs, especially Gemini 3.5 Flash, extracted colorectal cancer symptoms from discharge notes more accurately than rule-based or clinical NER methods.
clinical_relevance: This suggests LLM-based note review could help scale oncology symptom surveillance and reduce manual chart abstraction burden.
method: Analyzed 2,704 CRC discharge notes from MIMIC-IV.
Built a 46-symptom target list from MSAS and EORTC QLQ-CR29.
Compared dictionary rules, clinical NER, and zero-shot Claude/Gemini against a 200-note adjudicated gold standard.
evidence_signal: Against adjudicated ground truth, Gemini 3.5 Flash achieved Macro F1 0.70 and Micro F1 0.86, outperforming rule-based and NER approaches.
watch_item: Post-hoc negation filtering reduced LLM performance, highlighting the need for syntactic scope-aware validation before deployment.
paper_title: Leveraging Large Language Models for Colorectal Cancer Symptom Extraction from MIMIC-IV Clinical Notes
